questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The acedemic reputation and challenging myself.

Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, the information was given during a zoom meeting.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easu. I lived in a coop named Cloyne Court. I can recommend this as it is a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is cheaper, almost half the price of the on-campus accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for courses in July and enrolling is very competitive, meaning you have to be ready at a certain time and even then I still got waitlisted for some of my courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Berkeley International Office (BIO) is a great resource and also the website
berkeleytime.com
has a lot of information on courses and previous grade distributions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end i got of the waitlist and was able to enroll in the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look up courses you want to enroll in. A lot of courses are in the afternoon and evening, so make sure to check the class schedule. You can maybe have  no classes Monday and/or Friday for a 3-4 day weekend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The upperdivison BA (100-190) classes I took were easier than the equivalent in Copenhagen from my understanding. If I were to enroll again I would try to get a masters course (200-290) since I knew a lot of the course material already.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly it is very similar. Some courses have grade points for attending classes and discussions which is different from Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON C110
ECON C125
ECON 130
ECON 151

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ECON 130: Using Economics for Public Policy was a great course that covered a wide range of topics. The professor is young and friendly.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The SHIP health insurance was super expensive and I did not apply for a waiver. 15000 kr. for one semester. Try to apply for a waiver and get another form of insurance. Additionally, the fees of the visa appllication process ended up totalling almost 5000 kr.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In my coop food was included in the rent so i spent almost no money on food which was great.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every single thing you can imagine. So many different opportunities for students. Whether that is free gym access, sporting events, or kayaking for free on Saturdays.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a soccer tam and played in the IM league which was fun. Explore your passions and take advantage of all the resources.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can. Great national parks nearby in California. I visited Seattle and Las Vegas which was also fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Everyone was very approachable and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don-t be afraid to talk to the people next to you. A lot of people are looking to make new friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Living in a coop with a roommate it was sometime hard to get the privacy I was used to back home which was challenging at times.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Not being afraid to talk to strangers. People wil just start talking to you whether thats at a bar or at a restaurant or in an elevator.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go on hikes. The nature in the area is so beautiful
2. Go to the sport games. Especially the game against Stanford is an awesome experience.
3. Remember to enjoy it. The semester is short and time flies by so fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Students get free public transportation in the entire Bay Area. This is a great resource so take advantage.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and traveling with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
